text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Dedicated pool us-west-2-pool-7 p99 latency breach detected \u0026 streaming stalls observed. p95 ~ 720ms (normal 120ms), p99 ~ 3.2s. Queue depth spiked to 18k. Auto-scale attempted 3x but warmup delay > 90s. Paging: @Carla (SRE) oncall.

Carla (SRE): on it. grabbing dashboards and logs. Any recent deployment or maintenance in us-west-2? :eyes:

Ben (Runtime): we had a short kernel rollback earlier at 06:10 UTC (rolling patch to kernel-net) but that should be isolated to infra nodes not model hosts. I'll check runtime logs for kv-cache misses / cold-kv paths.

Alice (Support): getting customer reports: 6 distinct customers reported streaming stalls and partial responses, some 5xx errors. Frank (CS) pinged us - they flagged two high-traffic customers for SLA risk.

Frank (CS): Customers A & B (enterprise) saw degraded throughput. They're on Dedicated capacity. They called support. Need ETA and mitigation pls.

Carla (SRE): immediate mitigation plan: 1) reduce routing to us-west-2 for non-critical traffic; 2) enable fallback routing to compatible model-quantized variant in eu-west-1 for affected sessions; 3) attempt manual warmup of new nodes; 4) if autoscaler can't bring nodes up, we trigger reserved-burst where available. Assigning roles: @Ben (Runtime) check kv/cache warmup and streaming stalls; @Doug (Autoscale) check scale-controller logs and pool health; @Eve (Prod Eng) prepare temporary routing change.

Doug (Autoscale): looking at the controller: scale decisions fired at 06:21, 06:25, 06:29 UTC. New instance launches report "init: warmup_pending". Warmup step timed out at ~75s due to failing preflight: failed to fetch model shard metadata from NFS (I/O timeout). Autoscaler kept retrying but backoff caused effective delay ~ 90-120s. Logs: 

```
scale-controller: request_id=abc-6623 action=scale_up pool=us-west-2-pool-7 desired=8->16
node-launcher: node=instance-ww-42 status=provisioning
node-init: fetch-metadata error=IOTimeout path=/mnt/model-shard/meta.json
warmup: state=failed reason=kv-cache-warmup-timeout
```

Ben (Runtime): confirming: runtime shows a spike in `kv_miss_rate` and `kv_fetch_latency` at the same time. Streaming code path degenerates to synchronous shard fetch which blocks token emission => streaming stalls. We see the NFS gateway had brief rate-limiting due to concurrent fetches from warmup. Also notice model shard checksum mismatch retried twice then succeeded, added ~40s.

Eve (Prod Eng): OK — root cause hypothesis: combined effect of (1) scheduled infra kernel patch (reduced NFS throughput on some infra nodes) + (2) sudden traffic burst from Customer A running heavy batch tests triggered autoscale -> many warmups simultaneously hit the NFS metadata store causing timeouts and prolonged warmup. The autoscaler backoff made the delay visible at the API layer as queue depth growth.

Carla (SRE): mitigation actions executed: 
- Route non-enterprise traffic away from us-west-2 to reduce incoming load (done @06:43 UTC).
- Manual enqueue of warmup tasks staggered newly launched nodes to avoid NFS thundering herd (started @06:46 UTC).
- Enabled model-variant fallback for in-flight sessions with streaming fallback to quantized v-small (eu-west-1) for non-latency-critical calls (started @06:48 UTC).

Doug (Autoscale): manual intervention: I bumped pool capacity using reserved-burst tokens (temporary allotment) and forced warmup retries with increased concurrency limit for NFS fetches. New nodes came up around 06:58 UTC. Controller logs show stabilization after limiting parallel warmups.

Ben (Runtime): after staggered warmups, `kv_fetch_latency` dropped from 2.8s to ~120ms and `streaming_emit_rate` normalized. p99 dropped to ~220ms by 07:05 UTC. We still have elevated p95 for a handful of sessions that hit retry path.

Alice (Support): Notifying impacted customers with interim status: we advised Customer A & B about failover to eu-west-1 fallback and provided mitigation ETA. Customers asked for root cause summary and timeline.

Frank (CS): Customers accepted temporary routing for lower latency. They want postmortem and mitigation to avoid recurrence (esp around warmup at scale). Please assign postmortem owner.

Carla (SRE): I'll own the postmortem. Initial action items captured: 
- (SRE) Add warmup stagger heuristic to autoscaler (limit concurrent warmups per NFS gateway shard).
- (Runtime) Implement async KV prefetch pipelining to avoid blocking streaming path on a single fetch.
- (Infra) Investigate NFS gateway rate limits and add cache priming for common model shards.
- (Product) Evaluate routing policy to enforce global spillover earlier for dedicated pools under warmup stress.
- (Support/CS) Draft customer-facing timeline and RCA.

Doug (Autoscale): note: autoscaler currently exposes two knobs: `warmup_parallelism` (default 8) and `warmup_timeout` (default 60s). Immediate stopgap: lower `warmup_parallelism` to 3 for us-west-2-pool-7 and increase `warmup_timeout` to 120s. I'll push config change to pool config with a canary first.

Ben (Runtime): quick snippet of commands I ran: 
```
# check kv metrics
curl -s http://metrics.internal/us-west-2/pool-7 | jq '.kv_fetch_latency | select(.p99>1000)'
# tail streaming logs
kubectl logs -l app=runtime -n us-west-2 --since=2h | rg "kv_fetch|streaming_emit" -n
```

Carla (SRE): paging summary for handoff to @Maya (oncall-next): 
- Incident root cause: warmup thundering herd + NFS metadata fetch timeouts after infra kernel patch reduced throughput + sudden external traffic spike.
- Customer impact: two enterprise customers had streaming stalls and partial 5xxs from 06:20-06:58 UTC; degraded p99 until 07:05 UTC.
- Current status: pool stabilized, p99 back within SLO, manual mitigations in place (staggered warmup, reserved-burst, fallback routing).
- Open action items: warmup heuristics, async KV prefetch, NFS gateway hardening, autoscaler config changes, customer RCA.
- Postmortem owner: Carla (SRE). Expected draft in 48h.

Maya (oncall-next): thanks. I'll take handoff and monitor 2h. Any throttles or ongoing warmup failures to watch?

Doug (Autoscale): watching `warmup_failure_rate` and `scale_lag_seconds` for 1h. I left the pool in manual mode for now to avoid automated simultaneous warmups.

Ben (Runtime): leaving marker logs and tracing: trace-id=tr-6991234567-root will have all the streaming stall spans. Use that for the postmortem references.

Alice (Support): I'll follow up with CS to close the incident conversation with customers and share the timeline.

Frank (CS): appreciate the rapid mitigation. Please ping when postmortem is ready.

incident-bot: Incident status changed -> MONITORING. Severity: Sev2 -> reduced from Sev1 after mitigations.

Carla (SRE): closing thread for active triage. Will reopen if metrics regress. Thanks team. :heart:
